stem: Which of the following best describes the response of a rod photoreceptor to light?

opts.A: It depolarizes and fires an action potential
opts.B: It fires action potentials at a rate proportional to light intensity
opts.C: It hyperpolarizes and generates an action potential
opts.D: It remains at its resting potential
opts.E: It hyperpolarizes from its depolarized dark state without firing action potentials

stem: Which retinal cells are the first neurons of the visual pathway to generate action potentials, and give rise to the axons of the optic nerve?
A 28-year-old woman with a brain tumor and raised intracranial pressure has bilateral swelling of the optic discs. Which anatomic feature best explains this finding?

opts.A: The optic nerve is a peripheral nerve wrapped in endoneurium
opts.B: CSF communicates directly with the aqueous humor
opts.C: The optic nerve is covered by meninges with a subarachnoid space continuous with the intracranial one
opts.D: Optic nerve axons are myelinated by Schwann cells
opts.E: The central retinal artery arises from the anterior cerebral artery

stem: Which retinal fibers remain ipsilateral at the optic chiasm?

opts.A: Temporal retinal fibers, which carry the nasal visual field
opts.B: Nasal retinal fibers, which carry the temporal visual field
opts.D: All fibers from the inferior retina

stem: After a stroke, a 70-year-old man sees objects clearly and can describe their shape and color, but cannot name a key by looking at it. He identifies it immediately when he holds it. Which is the best description of this deficit?

opts.C: Visual agnosia from damage to association cortex

stem: Ptosis in Horner syndrome results from loss of sympathetic innervation to which muscle?

In the swinging flashlight test, both pupils constrict when light is shone in the left eye, but both pupils dilate when the light is swung to the right eye. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

opts.C: Afferent defect of the right eye or optic nerve (Marcus Gunn pupil)

stem: A patient with a dorsal pontine infarct has a right abducens nucleus lesion that also involves the right MLF. Which finding is expected?

opts.A: Both eyes are deviated to the left and cannot look right
opts.B: Left eye cannot abduct and right eye cannot adduct
opts.C: The right eye does not move horizontally, and the left eye can only abduct
opts.D: Both eyes move normally in horizontal gaze

stem: A patient shifts his gaze between two stationary fingers using jerky movements that place each finger on the fovea. Which movement is this?
Which anatomic observation best explains why light-near dissociation can occur in Argyll Robertson pupils?

opts.E: Partial damage to the pretectal area, which contains separate constrictor neurons for light and accommodation

stem: A person looks at a picture and sees balls of different colors, but they are all the same color. Which statement best explains the illusion?

opts.B: The brain interprets sensory input based on experience and expectation

stem: Which sequence correctly describes the flow of aqueous humor?

opts.A: Anterior chamber, then posterior chamber, then canal of Schlemm
opts.B: Ciliary body, then anterior chamber, then vitreous
opts.C: Ciliary body, then posterior chamber, then through the pupil to the anterior chamber, then trabecular meshwork and canal of Schlemm
opts.D: Choroid, then posterior chamber, then sclera
opts.E: Lens, then vitreous, then trabecular meshwork

stem: A newborn has no visible iris, nystagmus and foveal hypoplasia. Which gene is involved, and which tumor is associated with sporadic cases?
A 27-week premature infant is screened for retinopathy of prematurity. Which mechanism underlies the disease?

opts.D: Damaged retinal vessels induce VEGF release, causing abnormal vessel growth at the border of the vascular and avascular retina

stem: A 55-year-old man with long-standing diabetes has microaneurysms, cotton-wool spots and flame hemorrhages on fundoscopy. Which mechanism best explains the new vessel growth?

opts.B: Hyperglycemia damages capillaries, causing leakage and hypoxia that induces VEGF and fragile new vessels

stem: Where are the auditory receptor hair cells located?

opts.D: In the organ of Corti, between the basilar membrane and the overlying tectorial membrane

stem: Angular acceleration during head rotation is transduced by hair cells of the crista ampullaris, which are deflected by which structure?
Which feature allows the utricular macula to respond to gravity?

opts.E: Calcium carbonate crystals (otoconia) that weigh down the overlying gelatinous membrane

stem: In a comatose patient, rotating the head causes the eyes to remain fixed in space (an intact doll's eye reflex). What does this indicate?

opts.D: Intact vestibular nuclei and MLF connections to the CN III, IV and VI nuclei, which bypass the cortex

stem: Which pathway, when lesioned anywhere along its course, produces vertigo?

opts.D: Vestibulocerebellar fibers in the inferior cerebellar peduncle
opts.E: Vestibular nuclei to VPL thalamus to parietotemporal cortex

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes upper from lower motor neurons?

opts.A: UMN axons leave the CNS to synapse directly on muscle
opts.B: LMN cell bodies are located in the motor cortex
opts.C: UMN axons remain within the CNS and synapse on LMNs, whereas LMN axons leave the CNS to innervate muscle
opts.D: Both have axons in peripheral nerves
opts.E: LMNs are located only in the brainstem

stem: A 50-year-old man cannot clap his hands in the right rhythm after a stroke, yet his strength is normal. A lesion of which area is most likely?

opts.A: Premotor cortex or supplementary motor area
opts.C: Posterior limb of the internal capsule

stem: A patient has a lesion of the right lateral corticospinal tract at C3. What deficit is expected?

opts.C: Right spastic weakness below the lesion

stem: A patient after a large hemispheric stroke has flexed arms and extended legs. Where is the lesion?

opts.E: Motor cortex or descending fibers above the red nucleus

stem: A lesion of the left corticobulbar fibers at the level of the rostral medulla causes which of the following?

opts.A: Tongue deviates to the left with left facial droop
opts.D: Tongue deviates to the right with normal facial strength

stem: A 19-year-old woman has left LMN facial palsy and cannot close her left eye. Which treatment is most appropriate?

opts.B: Prednisone and eye protection with lubricant or patching

stem: A 60-year-old man has ear pain, vesicles in the ear canal, facial paralysis, vertigo and tinnitus. What is the cause?

opts.C: Varicella-zoster virus infection of CN VII (Ramsay Hunt syndrome)

stem: A child has fever followed by asymmetric flaccid paralysis, areflexia and normal sensation. Which structures are damaged?
A patient has a lesion of the left abducens nucleus. Which findings are expected?

opts.A: Right gaze palsy with right facial weakness
opts.E: Left gaze palsy with left facial weakness because facial nerve fibers loop around the nucleus

stem: A patient has a unilateral corticobulbar lesion. Which muscles remain normal because of bilateral cortical input?
Which mechanism allows the arcuate and periventricular nuclei to regulate the anterior pituitary?

opts.A: Their axons terminate directly in the anterior lobe
opts.B: Release of ADH from nerve terminals
opts.C: Direct neural control of pituitary acinar cells
opts.D: Release of hypophysiotropic hormones into the hypophyseal portal capillaries

stem: Which pathway links light exposure to melatonin release?

opts.A: Retina to LGN to occipital cortex to pineal gland
opts.B: Retina to pretectal area to Edinger-Westphal nucleus
opts.C: Retina to suprachiasmatic nucleus to a sympathetic pathway to the pineal gland
opts.D: Retina to ventromedial nucleus to pituitary
opts.E: Retina to mammillary bodies to pineal gland

stem: Which pair of nuclei makes up the striatum?
Which sequence describes the direct pathway?

opts.A: Putamen excites GPi, which inhibits the VL
opts.B: Putamen inhibits GPi, releasing VL from inhibition and exciting the motor cortex
opts.C: Putamen inhibits GPe, which inhibits the subthalamic nucleus
opts.D: Putamen excites GPe, which excites the VL
opts.E: Subthalamic nucleus excites GPi, which excites the VL

stem: Which sequence describes the indirect pathway?

opts.A: Putamen excites GPi, which excites the VL
opts.B: Putamen inhibits GPi, which excites the VL
opts.C: Putamen excites GPe, which excites the subthalamic nucleus
opts.E: Putamen inhibits GPe, disinhibiting the subthalamic nucleus, which excites GPi and inhibits the VL

stem: A schizophrenic patient on haloperidol for 5 years has lip smacking and tongue protrusion. Which mechanism is most likely?

opts.A: Dopamine depletion in the substantia nigra
opts.C: D2 receptor hypersensitivity causing excessive inhibition of the indirect pathway

stem: A 68-year-old man has neck and trunk rigidity, frequent backward falls, loss of voluntary vertical gaze, and a poor response to levodopa. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A man on rasagiline eats aged cheese and red wine and develops a severe headache with blood pressure of 210/120 mm Hg. What is the mechanism?

opts.D: Tyramine acting as a sympathomimetic that releases norepinephrine

stem: Which statement about benztropine in Parkinson disease is correct?

opts.E: It helps tremor but does not improve bradykinesia

stem: Which cellular mechanism is common to Parkinson, Huntington and ALS?

opts.C: Misfolded protein aggregation with impaired ubiquitin-proteasome turnover

stem: Which neurons promote wakefulness by inhibiting the VLPO?

opts.E: Orexin neurons of the lateral hypothalamus

stem: Which stage features muscle atonia, increased oxygen use and a wake-like EEG?
A 54-year-old woman has an uncomfortable sensation in her legs when she lies down that is relieved by walking. Which evaluation is most appropriate?
What is the mechanism of zolpidem?

opts.A: Binds GABA-A at the benzodiazepine site and facilitates chloride channel opening

stem: A patient with ALS has inappropriate laughing and crying. Which treatment is most appropriate?
Which statement about ALS is correct?

opts.A: About two-thirds of patients present with limb onset, and bulbar onset carries a worse prognosis
opts.C: Sensory loss is an early feature
opts.E: Extraocular muscles are the first to fail

stem: Which combination supports a diagnosis of ALS?

opts.C: Progressive UMN and LMN signs in different regions without sensory loss

stem: What is the rationale for edaravone in ALS?

opts.D: Blocking calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
opts.E: Scavenging free radicals, which counters oxidative damage linked to SOD1 mutations

stem: A patient has severe upper extremity spasticity that does not respond to oral agents. Which local therapy is appropriate, and how does it work?

opts.D: Botulinum toxin, which cleaves SNARE proteins and prevents vesicle release
